Mithril.js - vendored tailored ESM build
==========================================

Upstream:   https://mithril.js.org/
Version:    2.3.8
Source URL: https://unpkg.com/mithril@2.3.8/mithril.js  (UMD)
Reviewed:   2026-08-29
License:    MIT

Upstream UMD SHA-256:
  6c080d9a4b6289e32534bc2a0bab94cc864c5206f106bae4f8de96f4900b9960

Vendored tailored SHA-256 (mithril.js as committed):
  cccca61e4bafda5e4f49d5265f8ccafdc14b21a21f76796e18bef9728510a021

Notable changes since 2.2.2 (previous vendored version)
-------------------------------------------------------
- m.jsonp removed upstream — the API and its script-injection code no
  longer exist in the build at all (we already forbade it; see below).
- Internal Promise polyfill removed upstream. The build assumes a modern
  browser, which our MV3 target already guarantees.
- m.domFor added — new public API for iterating the DOM nodes a vnode
  rendered. Not used by us; not forbidden.

Tailoring
---------
`packaging/vendor-mithril.ts` fetches the exact upstream UMD, verifies its
SHA-256 and wrapper, then performs two narrow transformations:

1. Remove the UMD wrapper/export and append `export default m;`.
2. Remove the hash-pinned XHR request block and its `m.request` export.

The request block is bounded by unique exact anchors and has its own SHA-256
in the script. Any upstream drift fails closed for review. Every remaining
upstream body byte is preserved.

Classic App projection
----------------------
The source body is stored once. Extension pages import mithril.js directly.
Sandboxed Apps cannot resolve ES modules, so app-tab loads that same hash-locked
text and `mithril-classic-source.js` replaces the exact trailing
`export default m;` with `window.m = m` before compose. The exact-footer check
fails closed if an upstream update changes the conversion shape. Apps keep the
same `<script src="./mithril.js"></script>` contract without a duplicate vendor
body on disk.

Forbidden APIs (enforced by ESLint, see eslint.config.js)
---------------------------------------------------------
The following Mithril APIs are forbidden in this project. Importing or
referencing them is a lint error.

  m.request    — absent from the tailored build; it bypasses our safeFetch
                 egress allowlist and credential boundary
  m.jsonp      — same reason; would also load remote scripts. As of 2.3.x
                 this API is gone from upstream entirely; the ESLint rule
                 is kept as a tripwire in case a future bump reintroduces it.
  m.mount(document.body, ...)
               — mount only against named container elements; see §13.2

Why the tailored build stays narrow
------------------------------------
`m.request` is not merely unused: trusted extension IO must cross safeFetch,
while sandboxed Apps have no ambient network. Keeping an XHR path would expose
an API that has no valid peerd use. No other Mithril API is stripped. Peerd
owns the reproducible deletion recipe, not a rewritten renderer or router.

Update procedure
----------------
1. Audit the new upstream release and update the version, upstream SHA-256,
   and request-block SHA-256 in `packaging/vendor-mithril.ts`.
2. Run `bun packaging/vendor-mithril.ts --write`.
3. Read the generated diff and verify only the reviewed request subsystem and
   UMD wrapper/export are absent.
4. Record the new tailored SHA-256 and review date here.
5. Regenerate `vendor.lock.json`, then run the vendor and UI test suites.
